# Julia Performance Tracking (perf.julialang.org)

> Performance and health data for the Julia language, refreshed every 10 to 30 minutes: CI job and
> build timing from Buildkite (julia-ci master builds), Nanosoldier benchmark reports,
> PkgEval runs of the package ecosystem, TTFX (time to first X) of a set of package
> tasks on every master build and open pull request, the size of the binary distribution
> of master commits and open pull requests, package-server downloads, the Buildkite agents, and the
> issues, pull requests and commits of JuliaLang/julia.
> Everything lives in one SQLite database. The web pages are a JavaScript app; read the
> data in one of the four ways below instead of scraping them.

Pick by the size of the answer. All four are public, read-only and need no key.

## 1. The API: what a page of the site shows

`https://perf.julialang.org/api/` lists every route with its parameters and a
description; the list below is the routes an agent most often needs. All routes are GET
and return JSON; use `curl --compressed`. Routes with a `since` parameter return all
history without it, so pass it (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Responses carry an ETag: send it back as
`If-None-Match` to get a 304 when nothing changed, or poll `/api/status` first.

Commits:
- `/api/commit/<sha or PR number>`: everything for one master commit (CI jobs, TTFX and
  size against the previous commit and the releases, the first benchmark and PkgEval
  reports that include it), or for an open pull request, under `pr`, its TTFX and size
  against master and the releases
- `/api/commits?limit=100`: master commits, newest first
- `/api/status`: when each source last ingested successfully, and its change sequence; never cached, so poll this to see whether anything changed

CI timing:
- `/api/timing/builds?since=`: wall time and queue wait per master build
- `/api/timing/runs?since=`: every CI job run in the window (30 days is about 0.2 MB)

Benchmarks:
- `/api/benchmarks/summary`: the geomean of every benchmark group on every daily report, with its counts of regressions and improvements; the group names are the keys of each report's `by_group`
- `/api/benchmarks/groups/<group>?since=`: every benchmark of one group on every daily report, minimum and mean estimates
- `/api/benchmarks/verdicts?since=`: Nanosoldier's regressions and improvements
- `/api/notes/methodology_changes`: benchmarks whose measurement changed, where a step in the series is not a commit's

PkgEval:
- `/api/pkgeval/summary`: every daily report with its counts of ok, fail, crash, skip and kill
- `/api/pkgeval/package/<Name>`: one package's PkgEval status on every report
- `/api/pkgeval/changes`: packages that recently broke or were fixed on PkgEval and stayed so, with flaky flips filtered out
- `/api/pkgeval/reasons`: how many packages failed each way on the newest report
- `/api/pkgeval/failures?reason=precompile`: the packages failing for those reasons, by download rank, with how long each has failed
- `/api/pkgeval/popular`: the most downloaded packages that fail PkgEval, and for how long

TTFX:
- `/api/ttfx/summary?since=`: TTFX per task on every master build (times, including the load and run with every stdlib loaded first, invalidations and recompiled methods), and (`releases`) on the weekly runs of the newest stable release, and (`lts`) of the newest LTS release, and (`branch_nightly`) of the nightly of the next release's branch, and (`opt`) on the nightly optimized (PGO and ThinLTO) build, with `base`: the regular build of the same commit measured beside it
- `/api/ttfx/prs`: open pull requests ranked by their latest TTFX comparison against master, with whether CI passes on their head
- `/api/ttfx/job/<job_id>?task=`: one TTFX job's recompiled methods (from its trace logs) and invalidations with their top causes, per task
- `/api/notes/ttfx_annotations`: notes on TTFX jobs where the runners or the benchmark changed, so a step there is not a commit's

Runtime benchmarks:
- `/api/runtime/summary?since=`: about 110 runtime benchmarks (13 categories: scalar, simd, array, collections, strings, io, dispatch, types, runtime, gc, compiler, apps, parallel) on every master build: per benchmark the judged metric (cycles of the calling thread, or wall time), its spread over the job's blocks, retired instructions (exact, so a change means the code changed), wall time, allocations
- `/api/runtime/prs`: open pull requests by their latest runtime benchmark comparison against the merge-base, with per-category verdicts and the benchmarks that changed
- `/api/runtime/job/<job_id>`: one job's every benchmark with its per-block values
- `/api/runtime/run/<pipeline>/<build>/<job_id>`: any Runtime benchmarks job of julia-pr, julia-ci or julia-buildkite-ci, read from its Buildkite artifacts on first use: the arms, verdicts (and the confirmation run against a control build), per arm and block each benchmark's 5th-percentile value, quartiles, instructions and allocations; `?bench=<category/name>` gives that benchmark's samples. The page at `/runtime-run?pipeline=...&build=...&job=...` draws it
- `/api/notes/runtime_annotations`: notes on builds where the benchmark machine or suite changed, so a step there is not a commit's

Sizes:
- `/api/sizes/summary?since=`: size of the linux-x86_64 distribution (total, sys.so, pkgimages, runtime libraries) of master commits, back to 2020, and of every stable release since 1.10
- `/api/sizes/commit/<sha>`: one master commit's size against the previous measured commit, every metric and every file of at least 1 MiB
- `/api/sizes/prs`: the size of each open pull request's latest build against the master commit it branched from
- `/api/sizes/pr/<number>`: one open pull request's size against its merge-base, every metric and every file of at least 1 MiB

Sysimage:
- `/api/sysimage/summary?since=`: how long the build job of every master build spent making the system image, stage by stage (compiling the compiler, emitting basecompiler, Base, the sysimage's stdlibs, emitting sysbase, the precompile statements, emitting sys, then the stdlib pkgimages), per platform, from the job logs
- `/api/notes/sysimage_annotations`: notes on builds where how CI builds julia changed, so a step there is not a commit's

Downloads:
- `/api/downloads/top?days=7`: the 50 most requested packages over the window
- `/api/downloads/package/<Name>`: one package's daily downloads

Agents and GitHub:
- `/api/agents/backlog?since=`: per agent pool, the julia-pr and julia-ci jobs waiting for an agent and running over time, plus agents busy with other pipelines' jobs
- `/api/agents/usage?days=`: agent seconds of the julia-pr and julia-ci jobs finished in the last `days` (7 by default), per pipeline, job name, pool and state
- `/api/agents/build-hours?since=`: agent seconds, job count and outcome of every finished julia-pr and julia-ci build, the CI cost per pushed commit
- `/api/github/activity?since=`: JuliaLang/julia per day: open issues and pull requests, issues and pull requests opened, closed and merged, master commits, and contributors and time to merge over 30 days

The response shapes are the site's own and can change; the database schema is stable.

## 2. SQL: Datasette at /db/

`https://perf.julialang.org/db/ci-timing` answers read-only SQL. Each query is limited to
2 seconds and 5000 rows, and each client to 120 requests a minute, so aggregate in SQL
rather than paging through rows. The API allows 600 requests a minute per client.

- Every table and its main columns are described in
  `https://perf.julialang.org/db/-/metadata.json`.
- Saved queries for common questions (a job's duration by week, a package's PkgEval
  history, one TTFX task over time, ...) are listed under `queries` in
  `https://perf.julialang.org/db/ci-timing.json`. Run one as
  `/db/ci-timing/<name>.json?_shape=array&<parameter>=<value>`, e.g.
  `/db/ci-timing/package_pkgeval_history.json?_shape=array&package=DataFrames`.

```
curl -s -G https://perf.julialang.org/db/ci-timing.json \
  --data-urlencode "_shape=array" \
  --data-urlencode "sql=SELECT source, max(finished_at) FROM source_runs WHERE ok = 1 GROUP BY source"
```

## 3. The whole database

`https://perf.julialang.org/data/ci-timing.sqlite.gz` is the complete database, taken
once a week (about 300 MB, 900 MB unpacked). Download it once and query it with
`sqlite3` for anything that needs many queries or scans large tables such as
`bench_results` or `pkgeval_results`.

## 4. The extracts

`https://perf.julialang.org/data/<file>.json.gz` are the API's main shapes over all
history, rendered at most hourly, after an ingest that changed them: `timing_summary` (12 MB),
`benchmark_summary` and `benchmarks/<group>` (up to 3 MB each), `pkgeval_summary`,
`ttfx_summary`, `sizes_summary` (1 MB) and `packages_downloads_summary`. For a recent window,
the API with `since` is smaller. `analysis/fetch_data.jl` in the repository downloads them.

## Reference

- [Schema](https://github.com/JuliaCI/julia-ci-timing/blob/main/db/schema.sql): every table and column, with comments
- [Querying guide](https://github.com/JuliaCI/julia-ci-timing/blob/main/docs/querying.md): tables by topic and example queries
- [Repository](https://github.com/JuliaCI/julia-ci-timing): the fetchers, the API server and the site
- [Health](https://perf.julialang.org/healthz): per-source freshness and disk use

## Conventions

- Times are UTC ISO 8601 (`2026-09-22T13:41:50Z`). Durations are seconds, benchmark
  times nanoseconds, memory and sizes bytes. TTFX times are seconds, the minimum over the
  job's ABBA blocks.
- A ratio below 1, or a negative percentage, is faster or smaller. A TTFX pull request's
  score is a weighted geometric mean of its precompile, load, run and warm ratios against
  master (precompile and warm a third each, load and run a sixth each).
- A commit is identified by its full SHA where known; many older builds only have the
  8-character prefix (`builds.commit_prefix`).
- Benchmark and PkgEval reports run daily, not per commit; a commit's results
  are in the first report after it.
- Queue waits and build wall times exist only for builds since September 2026.
- To show a result, link the site with its view in the URL, for example
  `https://perf.julialang.org/commit?c=<sha>`, `/pkgeval?pkg=<Name>` or `/timing?t=30`.
